messages.author: Affairs and Order
messages.text:
<@1166065212537970722> correction to my numbers first: you already have universal healthcare, so your old-age deaths are 0.07%/h, not 0.1%. measured on the live ticks just now: capital -129k/h (gets 79k growth, loses 208k to old age), but your whole nation is actually still growing, +75k/h (808k growth vs 733k deaths). so the people aren't vanishing. the big provinces shrink a little and the small ones grow, because growth is split by cities/land and not by how many people already live there

on the 4.5B: there's no per-province max anymore since the 10-04 rebalance. that number is just your capital's weight for splitting growth, it's not a cap. the actual slowdown comes from a nation-wide comfort level, which is ~878M for you. you're at 4.03B (~4.6x over), so growth sits at the minimum floor. nothing caps you, it just grows really slowly past that point

what you can do: honestly not much is needed. it's ~0.015%/h on the capital, ~3M a day out of 856M. higher happiness and lower pollution raise your comfort a bit, and so do more cities/land, but those flatten out at your size

messages.author: Affairs and Order
messages.text:
<@1166065212537970722> no, your population isn't dying. the nation as a whole is still going up, about +75k/h. only the biggest provinces slowly lose people to the smaller ones, around 3M a day off the capital, which is ~0.35%/day

small correction to what was said above: buying more provinces/cities/land won't really change it at your size. your comfort is already maxed out (58k cities and 45k land, and the curve flattens after a few thousand), so your total growth stays at ~808k/h either way. I checked: even +5000 cities put straight into the capital only raises its share from ~79k/h to ~131k/h, still under the ~208k/h that dies of old age there. happiness is already 100%, and pollution (81% avg) only moves it by ~1%

so the short answer: nothing is broken on your side and you don't need to do anything. the capital will drift down slowly while the rest of the nation fills up
